title: Fifty-electron bit read by repeated non-destructive skipper sampling
idea: MINIFY the stored charge ~600x (from ~30,000 e- to ~50 e-): the storage node is a ~0.01 fF floating diffusion with no capacitor, and a per-subarray skipper-CCD-style floating-gate amplifier shuttles the packet under its sense gate N=16 times, averaging read noise below 1 e- rms before write-back.
why: Deletes the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and the AR 60-75:1 etch; cell heads toward 4F2 and write CV2 energy falls ~100x. Only viable if node leakage is pushed to ~1e-21 A (pair with a wide-gap or pinned node).

title: AlN-clad GaN quantum-well storage node with barrier-tilting write
idea: MAGNIFY the confining barrier from ~1 eV (Si junction) to ~2 eV by holding the bit as electrons in a 3-nm GaN well clad with AlN; a transfer gate transiently tilts the barrier with the help of the built-in polarization field (CCD-style transfer) to write in ~5 ns, and a HEMT channel beneath the well senses the stored charge non-destructively.
why: Thermionic escape falls by ~e^(-1 eV/kT) ~1e-17, so retention moves from 64 ms to hours and refresh (fact 3: 16-33% idle power, 10-20% bandwidth) nearly vanishes; no oxide tunneling, so endurance stays unlimited.

title: Polar-vortex superlattice dielectric with stabilized negative capacitance
idea: MAGNIFY effective permittivity ~10x by building the cell dielectric from 1-2 nm alternating lead-free BaTiO3/SrTiO3 layers whose polar vortices contribute a stabilized negative capacitance; the series stack nets k ~250-400 without hysteresis because the vortex state never fully switches.
why: Clears the k~70 requirement (fact 1) with margin, so capacitor AR could fall from ~70:1 to ~15:1, cutting etch steps and freeing height budget for tiers.

title: Four bits stacked in one pillar hole by depth segmentation
idea: MAGNIFY bits per etched hole 4x: form an AR-60 cylinder capacitor in an ONON-style mold, then interrupt the storage electrode with three ALD SiO2 plugs so four isolated segments sit at different depths, each reached by a ring-gate vertical-channel transistor patterned in the matching mold tier.
why: Reuses today's capacitor etch while placing 4 bits per hole, ~3x density without a 26-tier lateral 3D DRAM (fact 2); each ~1.2 fF segment needs a gain-cell or sensitive sense amp.

title: Three bits per cell via discharge-time encoding and shared TDC
idea: MAGNIFY levels per cell from 2 to 8: the cell discharges into the bitline through a precision current sink and a shared time-to-digital converter measures time-to-threshold (Q = I*t), turning tiny charge differences into ps-resolvable intervals; every refresh re-quantizes levels to cancel drift.
why: 3 bits per capacitor gives ~2.5x cost-per-bit gain net of extra periphery on the existing 6F2 process, no new materials or tools (facts 1, 4).

title: Goto-pair tunnel-diode latch storing bits at a quarter volt
idea: MINIFY hold voltage to ~0.25 V: two series Esaki band-to-band tunnel diodes grown as a vertical Ge/Si or GaSb/InAs stack form a bistable midpoint node (Goto pair) behind one access transistor, holding a static bit with ~10 pA standby and no refresh.
why: Escapes the ~1 V VARY / CV2 floor (fact 10) and refresh (fact 3); vertical diode stacking keeps area near 1T1C.

title: Snap-through buckled nanoribbon holds bits as geometry
idea: MINIFY a MEMS bistable beam to a 10 nm x 80 nm pre-stressed SiC or amorphous-carbon ribbon arched up or down; GHz-range resonance allows ~1 ns electrostatic snap-through writes, and position is read through the gap-capacitance change to an under-electrode.
why: Zero leakage, zero refresh, no capacitor wall (facts 1, 3); flip energy ~aJ; fatigue life of the ribbon is the open question.

title: Noncollinear antiferromagnet tunnel junction switched in picoseconds
idea: MAGNIFY switching speed to ~10 ps exchange timescales and MINIFY stray field to zero: the bit is the octupole order of Mn3Sn/Mn3Pt in an all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junction, written by spin-orbit torque and read by its tunnel magnetoresistance.
why: Unlimited magnetic endurance, no refresh, and no dipolar crosstalk so cells pack at ~2F spacing; DRAM-class latency with nonvolatility (facts 3, 9).

title: Many-electron polyoxovanadate clusters as molecular storage nodes
idea: MAGNIFY electrons per site: a grafted monolayer of tungsten-free vanadium/molybdenum polyoxometalate clusters on the storage electrode accepts ~6-12 electrons each at discrete redox steps, so a 20-nm node holds ~10x the charge of a same-footprint dielectric capacitor and can encode several levels.
why: Faradaic pseudo-capacitance breaks the charge wall (fact 1) and avoids the tungsten chokepoint; the risk is electron-transfer kinetics slower than 100 ns.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM with a tenfold smaller capacitor
idea: MINIFY temperature to 77 K: subthreshold and junction leakage drop >1e6, so retention reaches minutes even with Cs = 0.5 fF; capacitor AR falls from ~70:1 to ~7:1 and refresh nearly disappears, deployed as LN2-immersed rack sleds.
why: Hits facts 1 and 3 together: fewer high-AR steps (~20-30% cheaper cell process), refresh energy ~0; cooling overhead amortized at datacenter scale.

title: Kinetic-inductance nanowire loop storing a single flux quantum
idea: MINIFY the superconducting memory loop from ~10 um2 to ~0.1 um2 by replacing geometric inductance with NbN nanowire kinetic inductance; a bit is one circulating fluxon, written and read by nanocryotron (nTron) gates at 4 K.
why: Zero static power, ps access, unlimited endurance for cryogenic AI and quantum controllers, with density approaching DRAM at 4 K (facts 3, 5).

title: Vertical charge-coupled shift-register strings replace per-cell transistors
idea: MAGNIFY charge transfer and MINIFY contacts: bits are charge packets clocked along vertical poly-Si CCD channels formed in 3D-NAND-style holes with 64 gate tiers; each string has one inject/sense contact at the top, so storage sites need no access transistor or capacitor.
why: 3D stacking with a NAND-like process (fact 2) and much less periphery (fact 7); average latency ~32 shifts x 0.5 ns = 16 ns, needs charge-transfer inefficiency < 1e-5.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous metal sponge multiplies capacitor surface tenfold
idea: MAGNIFY electrode area: deposit a Ru-Al or Ti-Al alloy liner in a shallow capacitor hole, selectively leach the Al to leave a metal sponge with 3-5 nm pores, then coat with ALD ZrO2 and a plate electrode, giving ~10x the internal surface of a smooth cylinder.
why: Same ~5 fF at AR ~10:1 instead of 70:1 (fact 1), removing the hardest etch and making capacitors stackable; conformal dielectric inside the pores is the risk.

title: Solid-electrolyte double-layer nanocapacitor with Helmholtz-scale gap
idea: MAGNIFY areal capacitance ~100x with an electric double layer: a 3-nm solid proton conductor (hydrated ZrO2 or phosphosilicate glass) between blocking electrodes stores charge in a ~0.5-nm Helmholtz layer (~10-20 uF/cm2), so a planar 20x20 nm node reaches ~0.08 fF, enough for a gain-cell read gate with no high-AR etch.
why: Removes the capacitor etch (fact 1, fact 4 capital); ionic relaxation at nm thickness must reach < 100 ns.

title: Avalanche-multiplying read transistor amplifies sub-femtofarad nodes
idea: MAGNIFY read signal 50-100x: the gain-cell read device is an impact-ionization MOS (I-MOS) biased just below breakdown only during read, so ~0.05 fF of stored gate charge switches avalanche on or off with a sub-5 mV/decade slope.
why: Lets Cs shrink ~50x (fact 1) and cuts read energy; hot-carrier wear is bounded because the avalanche bias is applied ~1e-9 of the time.

title: On-chip gigahertz phononic delay loop recirculating bits in flight
idea: MAGNIFY frequency and MINIFY wavelength of 1940s mercury delay-line memory: 20 GHz acoustic pulses travel ~4 km/s in thin-film LiNbO3 or AlScN waveguides, so a 1-mm spiral holds ~5 us x 20 Gb/s = 100 kbit, regenerated by a piezo transducer and comparator at each loop end.
why: ~1e8 bit/mm2 with no cell, no capacitor and no EUV (facts 1, 4); energy only spent regenerating; suits sequential tiers such as streaming KV caches.

title: Charge-density-wave domain switching in 1T-TaS2 picosecond bit
idea: MAGNIFY speed and MINIFY energy: a 10-nm 1T-TaS2 film is switched by a ~30 ps electrical pulse into a metastable hidden charge-density-wave domain state (~1000x resistance change) and erased by a longer pulse; run in a ~200 K module where the metastable state lasts seconds to hours, giving refresh-light dynamic memory.
why: ~fJ writes, ps speed, non-destructive resistive read (fact 8) and no atomic motion so endurance may be unlimited.

title: Antiferroelectric-biased capacitor rides the steep switching slope
idea: MAGNIFY dQ/dV: a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor is pre-biased by the plate to just below its AFE-to-FE field, so the 0/1 swing traverses the field-induced transition and charge per volt rises ~3-4x; with no remanence the film relaxes back each cycle, avoiding wake-up and imprint.
why: Effective k ~100-150 (fact 1) so the capacitor can be ~3x shorter; hysteresis loss and transition fatigue are the risks.

title: Nanometre proton-intercalation channel bit with nanosecond writes
idea: MINIFY the ion path to ~2 nm: a gain-cell read channel of MoO3 or Nb2O5 sits on a sub-5-nm solid proton reservoir; a 1-2 V, 5 ns gate pulse moves protons in or out, shifting channel conductance ~10x for non-destructive reads, with retention set by reservoir barrier thickness.
why: Capacitor-free (fact 1), non-destructive read (fact 8), tungsten-free; endurance must clear ~1e12 cycles to play the DRAM role.

title: Quantum-paraelectric strontium titanate planar capacitor at 77 K
idea: MAGNIFY permittivity through quantum paraelectricity: SrTiO3 near 77 K has bulk k ~1000-1500; a strain-engineered 5-nm film on a SrRuO3 electrode that keeps k >= 300 makes a flat 20x20 nm capacitor of ~0.2-0.7 fF, enough with cryogenic retention.
why: Flat, etch-free capacitor replaces the AR 70:1 pillar (fact 1) and its litho/etch steps (fact 4); interfacial dead layer is the main risk.

title: Microsecond-retention parasitic-node bit for streaming activations
idea: MINIFY retention on purpose from 64 ms to ~10 us: store bits only on the ~0.05 fF parasitic node of a capacitor-less vertical transistor and map the tier to AI activations and KV staging data that live < 10 us, so data is consumed before it decays and refresh never runs.
why: Drops capacitor and refresh (facts 1, 3); a transistor-only ~4F2 cell gives ~3x density for scratch buffers.

title: Threshold-switch-gated crosspoint capacitor without access transistor
idea: MINIFY the cell to a 4F2 crosspoint: each capacitor is in series with a Mott threshold switch (NbO2 or doped VOx) that is insulating below ~0.8 V and conducting above, so only fully selected cells charge or discharge while half-selected ones stay sealed; decks stack 8+ high using only deposition and line patterning.
why: No transistor, monolithic 3D stacking (fact 2) on mature-litho lines (fact 4); threshold-switch off-leakage may limit retention to ms.

title: Nanorelay-gated storage node with effectively infinite off-resistance
idea: MAGNIFY access-device off-resistance to infinity: replace the access transistor with a ~1 ns, 15-nm-gap NEMS contact switch (Ru or TiN cantilever) so the storage node is isolated by a gas gap when open and only the capacitor dielectric leaks.
why: Kills the leakage tail (fact 3) for hours-to-days retention and lowers wordline voltage via ~1 V pull-in (fact 10); contacts must survive ~1e14 cycles.

title: Anodized-alumina 1000:1 pore capacitor forest on foundry CMOS
idea: MAGNIFY aspect ratio to ~1000:1 with a beaker: sputter Al onto finished foundry CMOS wafers, anodize it into self-ordered 20-40 nm pores, then ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN inside; each 250-nm landing pad catches ~30 pores so no pore-to-cell alignment is needed. Tools: an anodization bath, one ALD tool and one contact litho.
why: Cs > 5 fF per cell without plasma high-AR etch (fact 1) and with tiny capital (fact 4); turns mature-node logic into embedded DRAM.

title: Display-fab DRAM panels: magnify area, minify cost per area
idea: MAGNIFY substrate area ~1000x and MINIFY cost per m2: a 10-person team designs 1T1C arrays of oxide or LTPS TFTs at ~3 um pitch and buys Gen-8.5 glass runs from idle LCD fabs; a 5.5 m2 sheet of ~10 um2 cells holds ~70 GB raw, diced into slabs bonded to logic by panel-level fan-out.
why: Zero EUV and uses depreciated display capital (fact 4), ally-sourced capacity; at ~$10-20/GB it serves a slower 100-ns tier, not the hottest DRAM.

title: Pinned-photodiode buried node borrowed from image-sensor foundries
idea: MAGNIFY retention by holding the bit in a fully depleted, surface-pinned buried n-well (a CIS pinned photodiode kept dark, dark current ~1-10 e-/s) with a transfer gate and source-follower readout like a global-shutter pixel memory, taped out on a commercial CIS MPW.
why: Retention of seconds to minutes at ~2,000 e- cuts refresh energy and bandwidth >100x (fact 3) on a known foundry process; ~0.5-1 um2 cells suit low-power embedded tiers.

title: Light-powered self-refreshing photo-latch cell under an LED flood
idea: MAGNIFY the refresh source from a controller to photons: each cell adds a tiny photodiode feeding its storage node through a transistor gated by that node, so under uniform LED illumination '1' nodes keep topping themselves up while '0' nodes stay shut, a bistable cell needing no refresh commands; built on a CIS MPW.
why: Removes refresh commands and the 10-20% bandwidth tax (fact 3); the photocurrent needed only has to beat ~13 fA, so LED power is negligible.

title: Vanadium dioxide hysteresis bit parked inside its transition loop
idea: MINIFY the thermal window: hold a sputtered VO2 cell array at the midpoint of its ~5-10 K metal-insulator hysteresis with a chip thermostat; a forward current pulse through a VO2/Bi2Te3 junction Peltier-heats a 30-nm cell onto the metallic branch, and a reverse pulse Peltier-cools it back onto the insulating branch, read by resistance.
why: Static, refresh-free, non-destructive read (facts 3, 8) built with two sputter targets; local Peltier cooling strength is the weak point.

title: Lithium-niobate domain-wall conduction bit on purchased LNOI wafers
idea: MINIFY the readout to a domain wall: on commercial thin-film lithium-niobate-on-insulator, a ~1-2 V pulse between surface electrodes nucleates a nanoscale inverted domain whose charged walls conduct ~nA; read non-destructively at sub-coercive voltage, erased by reverse pulse. Needs only a stepper, metal lift-off and an etcher.
why: Non-destructive read (fact 8), nonvolatile so no refresh (fact 3), LN wall cells have shown >1e10 cycles; minimal tooling.

title: Leaky floating gate with direct-tunneling oxide for unlimited writes
idea: MINIFY the tunnel oxide to ~2.5 nm so writes use direct tunneling at ~2 V in ~10 ns instead of damaging Fowler-Nordheim injection, accepting seconds-to-hours retention; a 10-person team runs it on a 180-nm university or MPW-compatible flow with a poly floating gate.
why: Quasi-volatile memory refreshed ~1000x less than DRAM (fact 3), capacitor-free (fact 1), endurance >1e12 because direct-tunnel stress is low; U.S. mature-node manufacturable.

title: Long-channel thick-oxide gain cell in open-source 130 nm
idea: MAGNIFY channel length ~10x and oxide thickness ~3x on the write device: a 3T gain cell in the open SKY130/GF180 PDKs uses the 5 V thick-oxide transistor as write switch (aA subthreshold leakage) and stores on the read transistor's gate; free or cheap shuttles allow monthly iterations.
why: Retention ~1-10 s vs 64 ms (fact 3) in U.S.-fabbed nodes with near-zero capital; niche embedded DRAM for chiplets.

title: Self-assembled BaTiO3 nanocube ink as a spin-coated high-k
idea: MAGNIFY permittivity by printing it: hydrothermally synthesized 10-15 nm single-crystal BaTiO3 nanocubes self-assemble from ink into dense superlattices on the bottom electrode, then an ALD infill densifies the film without high-temperature sintering, targeting k ~100-200.
why: k well above 70 (fact 1) without perovskite MOCVD/ALD capital; the low-k infill in series is the risk.

title: Photonic-crystal nanocavity bistable bits in a silicon photonics foundry
idea: MINIFY optical bistable memory from fiber loops to ~1 um3 photonic-crystal nanocavities whose carrier-plasma bistability holds a bit at tens of nW bias; designed by a small team on a photonics MPW and written/read by wavelength-multiplexed light on the same bus used for chip-to-chip optical I/O.
why: Memory sits on the optical interconnect, cutting data-movement energy (fact 5) for photonic accelerators; no capacitor or EUV.

title: Midpoint-bootstrapped stacked switch nulls storage-node leakage
idea: MINIFY the voltage across the leakage path to millivolts: the write switch is split into two series transistors and their midpoint is driven by a small feedback transistor from the read device that mirrors the stored level, so the inner switch sees ~0 V drain-source during hold (a sample-and-hold trick applied per cell).
why: Leakage 100-1000x lower so retention reaches seconds (fact 3) in any foundry node; a 4T cell designable by a small team.

title: Silicon-carbide CMOS foundry DRAM for 200 C environments
idea: MAGNIFY bandgap from 1.1 to 3.3 eV using a commercial 4H-SiC CMOS MPW: 1T1C or gain cells whose intrinsic carrier density is ~1e-8 cm^-3 (vs 1e10 in Si) retain data at 200 C longer than silicon DRAM does at 25 C; a small team sells into down-hole, aerospace and EV-inverter markets.
why: Refresh-light memory at extreme temperatures (fact 3), U.S. SiC fabs, no EUV; pulls niche demand off silicon DRAM.

title: Gate-leakage load latch: engineered leakage holds static bits
idea: MAGNIFY a parasitic into the mechanism: in a 2-transistor cell on thin-oxide foundry devices, gate-tunneling current of one transistor acts as a pA pull-up and subthreshold current of the other as pull-down; sized so their I-V curves cross three times, the node has two stable voltages and holds statically.
why: No refresh (fact 3) at roughly half the area of 6T SRAM, designable on a 65/28 nm MPW; tight process variation control is required.

title: Sputtered complementary-oxide SRAM layer stacked over any chip
idea: MINIFY the fab to a sputter tool: room-temperature sputtered p-type SnO and n-type ZnSnO thin-film transistors form cross-coupled 6T latches above finished foundry CMOS; repeat the 4-mask module to stack several memory layers.
why: Static, refresh-free memory in monolithic 3D without EUV (facts 2, 4), all-U.S. tools; p-oxide mobility limits access to ~10-50 ns.

title: Self-boosting MOS varactor capacitor doubles read charge
idea: MAGNIFY the signal with a nonlinear capacitor: the storage capacitor is a MOS varactor whose inversion threshold sits between the '0' and '1' levels, so a stored '1' is in high-capacitance inversion and a '0' in low-capacitance depletion; a plate pulse at read delivers ~2-3x the bitline charge difference of a linear capacitor of equal area.
why: Smaller capacitor for the same sense margin (fact 1) in any mature foundry eDRAM; smaller CV2 swing.

title: Thousand-composition sputter library hunts for k-over-100 dielectrics
idea: MAGNIFY experiment throughput ~1000x: co-sputter three targets with deliberate thickness gradients onto one 150-mm wafer pre-patterned with 1,000 MIM test capacitors, then auto-probe k, leakage at 1 V and breakdown overnight, screening ternary oxide spaces such as Ti-Zr-La-O weekly.
why: A fast, cheap route to k >= 70 at <= 1e-7 A/cm2 (fact 1) without big-fab capital.

title: Two-hundred-variant bit-cell zoo on every shuttle run
idea: MAGNIFY variants and MINIFY cost per experiment: tile 200 bit-cell variants (gain cells, varactor caps, bootstrapped switches, leakage latches) with on-die retention/endurance BIST on each $10-20k MPW shuttle, publish an open retention-tail database and license the winners.
why: Cuts cell-discovery cycles from years to quarters and feeds U.S. fabs with characterized cells (facts 3, 4).

title: Half-inch Minimal Fab runs a full 1T1C process on desks
idea: MINIFY the fab: run a planar or trench 1T1C process on 12.5-mm wafers with desk-sized Minimal Fab tools (maskless litho, per-tool local cleanroom, ~$5-20M total), so a 10-person team iterates storage-element materials in days instead of waiting for foundry lots.
why: Capital intensity ~1000x lower for R&D and small-batch defense or rad-hard memory (fact 4, U.S. manufacturability).

title: Harvest and re-bin DRAM dies from retired server DIMMs
idea: MAGNIFY the life of existing storage elements: a small reverse-logistics shop buys decommissioned DDR4 DIMMs, retention-tests every die at elevated temperature, re-bins by refresh class and rebuilds CXL memory expanders whose controller applies per-die refresh rates.
why: Raises usable supply without new wafers during the shortage; cost per bit near scrap value plus test.

title: Nanoimprint master replicates capacitor hole arrays without EUV
idea: MINIFY litho cost per layer: e-beam write one 20-nm-hole master, then UV-nanoimprint the storage-node hole layer wafer after wafer with a ~$2M tool; periodic hole arrays are the ideal imprint case because overlay tolerance is loose.
why: Replaces 1-2 EUV exposures on the storage node (fact 4: depreciation ~55% of wafer cost) with tooling a small team can own.

title: Gated lateral thyristor latch in thin SOI foundry
idea: MINIFY the bistable to one gated PNPN body: in a 45/22 nm SOI MPW, a lateral thyristor with a capacitively coupled gate holds '1' by regenerative latching and '0' by blocking, with ~nA holding current and ~1-2 ns gate-pulse writes; no capacitor, no refresh.
why: Static cell at ~8-12F2, about 5x denser than SRAM (fact 3 avoided); standby current is the trade.

title: Barrier-free spin-orbit bit read by anomalous Hall cross
idea: MINIFY the magnetic stack to three sputtered layers with no tunnel barrier: a perpendicular Co dot on a Pt Hall cross is switched by spin-orbit torque from in-plane current and read by its anomalous Hall voltage with a differential sense amp, needing one litho step and one sputter run.
why: Unlimited magnetic endurance and nonvolatility in a process a small team owns; ~mV signal favors cache-sized arrays.

title: Parametron revival: bits as phase of MEMS parametric oscillators
idea: MINIFY Goto's 1954 ferrite parametron to ~5-um AlN resonators from a MEMS foundry: a 2f pump makes each resonator oscillate at f with phase 0 or pi (the bit), held while pumped and copied by coupling; majority-vote coupling adds in-memory logic.
why: Bit storage with no charge, no leakage tail and native compute-in-memory (facts 3, 5); low density makes it a rad-hard niche product.
